words.definition: A lucky discovery made by chance.
words.example: Finding that old note was pure serendipity.

words.definition: Focused on practical results instead of theory.
words.example: She took a pragmatic approach to learning.
His eloquent speech won everyone over.

words.definition: Able to recover quickly from difficulty.
words.example: The resilient team kept improving after setbacks.

In a sitting position; having taken a seat.
words.example: The audience was seated before the performance began.

words.definition: To sit or rest on a high or narrow place, often with a sense of balance.
words.example: She perched on the edge of the balcony to watch the parade.

words.definition: The position in which someone holds their body while standing or sitting, reflecting health and confidence.
words.example: Good posture can prevent back pain.

words.definition: To pause from activity and relax, often to regain energy.
words.example: After the long hike, he took a rest in the shade.

words.definition: To become fixed in a position or to resolve a dispute.
words.example: The children settled into their seats as the teacher entered.

words.definition: To take up space, time, or a position, or to hold a role.
words.example: The new museum will occupy the old warehouse.

words.definition: To organize or put in order, often to prepare for an event.
words.example: She arranged the chairs in a semicircle for the workshop.

words.definition: A long seat for multiple people, usually found in parks, schools, or sports venues.
words.example: They sat on the bench in the park.

words.definition: A seat with a back and legs, designed for one person to sit comfortably.
words.example: She sat in the chair at the conference.

words.definition: A particular place or arrangement of something, often used to describe where someone sits or stands.
words.example: She found a comfortable position on the sofa.
